To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) ActA is secreted by esophageal keratocytes in response to acid and bile salt exposure, 2) ActA is required for bile salt and acid-mediated keratocyte proliferation and migration, and 3) ActA induces de-differentiation of esophageal keratiocytes in response to bile salts and acid exposure.
Activin A (a cytokine involved in inflammation) is involved in the repair of esophageal tissue in a model of gastroesophagea reflux disease (GERD).
Activin A-mediated epithelia de-differentiation plays a role in the injury repair in an esophagitis model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the TGFβ superfamily member Activin A in the inflammatory response to gastroesophageal acid and bile exposure.
understanding the mechanisms that regulate epithelial de-differenceiation and repair in response to gastroesophageal injury.
the role of ActA in esophageal injury and repair, and its potential role in the development of Barrett's esophagus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our results support the notion that ActA is a key regulator of esophageal epithelial repair in the GERD environment.
our findings support the concept that ActA-mediated epithelial de- differentiation contributes to injury repair and tissue regeneration in a GERD model.
ActA-mediated de-differentiation of the esophageal keratincytes contributes to injury repair and may be a potential target for the prevention of GERD and the development of Barrett's esophagus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ActA is a novel mediator of GERD-induced esophageal epithelial injury, repair and metaplasia.
ActA is involved in epithelial de-differenciation, which contributes to injury repair and healing.
Activin A is a novel regulator of epithelial de-diffentiation and repair in the context of GERD injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the TGFβ signaling molecule Activin A is an essential component of the esophageal response to acid/bile exposure and that it is involved in epithelial de-diffentiation and repair of reflux-induced damage.
Activin A may be a novel target for the treatment of GERD.
ActA is a key player in the inflammatory environment of gastroesophageous reflux disease (GERD).
